title: Chess, But My Pieces Have Magnets
summary: Chess vs Stockfish where every White piece carries a magnet that attracts LIKE pieces (same piece type) it currently attacks. When one of your pieces attacks an enemy piece of the same type (bishop sees bishop, knight sees knight, rook sees rook on an open file, queen sees queen), you can pull that enemy piece one square toward you, dragging it out of its defences so it can be captured for free. Pawns' magnets are decorative (pawns only attack adjacent). Narrator wins a bishop early, later more material via the rook on the c-file, and wins by promotion + ladder mate.
rules: Standard chess start; player White vs Stockfish (3600). Only White has magnets.

Magnet power: if a white piece attacks an enemy piece of the same type, the player may attract it: the enemy piece is moved one square toward the attacking piece along the line/path of attack (e.g. bishop on d6 pulled to e5).
Using the magnet is the player's action for that turn [inferred], after which the pulled piece can be captured by any of your pieces next turn (not necessarily the magnet piece).
Knights can pull knights from an L-shape attack [direction of pull for knights not specified - inferred: to the square adjacent toward the attacker].
Pawn magnets do nothing (pawns only attack adjacent squares).
No limit on number of uses mentioned.

current_impl_issues: Legacy 'magnets': every moved piece automatically pulls enemy pieces two squares away one step closer - wrong. Real: only same-type enemy pieces your piece attacks can be pulled, by player choice.
